LESSON: SIGN READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: SIMPLE POEMS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive sign reading: Simple poems
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive sign reading: Simple poems, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are poems different from stories? 2. Why would you use a poem instead of a story to pass a message?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive sign reading: Simple poems together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy : Learners develop the skill of effective communication as they present ideas with confidence and recite poems.

Values:
● Peace: is enhanced as learners work with empathy in teams during the poetry recitation.

● Social justice: is developed as learners recite poems that promote fairness in society.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the skills of recitation to performance techniques in other learning areas such as Creative Arts.
